The statement signals a shift toward easier policy with a 50 bp cut while maintaining balance‑sheet runoff, which aligns with flexible inflation‑forecast targeting (Svensson) and interest‑rate rule frameworks (Taylor; Woodford) that call for lower policy rates as the inflation gap narrows and labor‑market momentum cools. Continued QT and data‑dependent language help preserve credibility against time‑inconsistency and inflation‑bias risks (Barro–Gordon; Rogoff), supporting anchored expectations in a New Keynesian Phillips‑curve setting where expected inflation is pivotal. The operating details—recalibrated administered rates (IORB/ON RRP), standing facilities, and runoff caps—reflect modern implementation practice documented by Goodfriend and Meulendyke and keep some restraint via term‑premium channels even as the policy rate declines. Net assessment from this literature is cautiously positive: progress toward target inflation and balanced risks improve the macro‑financial outlook, tempered by residual inflation uncertainty and ongoing balance‑sheet tightening.
